title: Security sync - field notes and triage log
content:
Meeting: Security Engineering weekly sync (informal notes)
Date: 2027-02-09
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel, Lena Morales, Samir Gupta, Eve Nakamura, (brief drop-ins: Jo Ramos, oncall SRE)

Purpose: quick weekly alignment across vuln triage, secrets posture, and ongoing threat modeling for Private deployments. This doc captures raw notes, unanswered questions, and action items — not a polished summary.

AGENDA (running):
- Rapid vuln triage updates (top items, owners, mitigation status)
- Secrets scanning and rotation cadence (recent incidents and gaps)
- Threat modeling sync: Private deploy surface changes (KMS/HSM flows)
- Open blockers and follow-ups for next week

1) Vulnerability triage snapshot
- RED-5412: third-party dependency chain (rust crate) flagged by OSS scanner with moderate severity (path traversal possibility in 3rd-party crate used by internal tooling). Current status: patch available upstream; patch PR created by infra team to vendor the safe version (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/289). Owner: Arjun. Risk: medium for tooling only (not user-facing), but could impact on-prem build steps.
  - Immediate mitigation: CI gating rule added to reject builds with vulnerable crate until PR merges (temporary). Action: Arjun to coordinate backport and notify release engineering (ETA 2027-02-11).

- RED-5667: memcache misconfiguration discovered during penetration test (staging). Exposes metrics and could be used to enumerate user IDs. Owner: Lena. Risk: high in staging; low in production (prod already behind firewall but we need parity).
  - Decision: Harden default memcache settings on all envs, update cloud init templates for Private images. Action: Lena to open infra change (CHANGE-1182) and schedule for 2027-02-15 maintenance window.

- New low-severity web-framework XSS warning in internal admin UI (scanner noisy). Owner: Samir to validate false positive.
  - Samir: quick audit suggests it's input sanitization gap in legacy admin form. He will file a small PR to encode outputs; estimate 1-2 dev days. Due 2027-02-16.

- Notes on prioritization: we re-affirmed rule-of-thumb: anything that affects customer data or auth flows gets priority over tooling-level CVEs. Keep clear callouts in Jira tickets about data exposure risk.

2) Secrets posture and rotation
- Recent finding: one rotated service account key found in a private gist (identified by automated scanner). Leak age ~6 hours before detection. This is the second small leak this quarter.
  - Immediate response: key is revoked (Eve) and replacement created; rotation documented in secrets inventory (Confluence). Root cause: developer used quick repro step and pasted temporary key to gist to share with contractor.
  - Lessons: enforce ephemeral secret sharing via internal secure-share tool; remove ability to create long-lived service account keys for dev accounts.

- Rotation cadence proposal (quick brainstorm):
  - Short-lived tokens for builders (tokens expire in 24 hours)
  - Service accounts that must be long-lived: enforce automated rotation every 30 days with audit logs and mandatory owner.
  - Enforcement plan: IAM policy changes + CI pre-commit hooks + automated scanner that auto-notifies owner and rotates keys if found in public.
  - Action: Eve to draft formal change request and rollout plan by 2027-02-18; include comms template for developers.

- Secrets scanning false positives: some internal swagger examples contain base64 inlined certs flagged; we need an allowlist mechanism per repo to reduce noise. Action: Samir to propose allowlist rules by 2027-02-14.

3) Threat modeling for Private deployments (ongoing)
- Context: customers adopting Private deployment request bring-your-own-KMS and optional on-prem HSMs. New threat surfaces: key egress during lifecycle operations, misconfiguration of network peering, and local admin controls.

- Discussion points:
  - KMS integration: design to support customer-managed KMS without exposing key material to Redwood control plane. Proposed approach: key wrapping — we never persist plaintext model keys; we keep only wrapped keys and include audit hooks.
  - E2E flow sketch (notes):
    - Customer creates key in their KMS (external)
    - They provide a key handle to Redwood via secure onboarding API
    - Redwood performs asymmetric wrap operation and stores only the wrapped payload; all crypto ops delegated to customer KMS during runtime via secure channels
  - Open question: does the onboarding API need to support HSM-to-HSM attestation? Likely yes for high-compliance customers.
  - Action: Maya + Lena to draft threat model diagram and list of control requirements for HSM attestation by 2027-02-23.

- Attack scenarios captured quickly:
  - Attacker with network access to Private control plane tries to exfiltrate wrapped keys; risk mitigations: strict RBAC, mTLS between runtime and KMS, attestation logs, and zero-trust network segmentation.
  - Insider threat: operator with access to control plane attempts to request key unwraps. Mitigation: require multi-party approval for unwrap operations for high-class keys (policy).

4) Observability and post-incident review items
- We still lack a convenient dashboard for secret-rotations and key revocation events. Current data is scattered across Cloud IAM audit logs, internal inventory, and rotation scripts.
  - Quick fix: build a centrally aggregated Lambda that writes normalized rotation events to our observability pipeline (OTEL -> logging index). Owner: Jo Ramos (SRE) with input from Eve. Proposal due 2027-02-17.

5) Open blockers / dependencies
- Legal sign-off required for the new Private KMS onboarding API language (privacy + liability). Legal contact: Priya Kaur. Maya to ping Legal for draft review (target 2027-02-20).
- Release engineering dependency: vendor patching workflow needs to be tested in canary before we push fix for RED-5412. Release eng owner: Tom B. Arjun to coordinate.

6) Quick incident retrospective notes (secret leak event)
- Timeline: leak 발견 -> scanner alert -> key revoked within ~2 hours -> replacement key issued -> incident comms to involved parties.
- What worked: scanner detected public gist quickly; automation revoked keys on callout; owner contact list worked.
- What to improve: reduce manual steps for revoking and provisioning replacements (automation), and reduce cognitive load on devs who are sharing secrets in ephemeral ways.

7) Action items (concrete)
- Arjun: finish PR to vendor rust crate + coordinate canary test with release engineering (RED-5412). Due 2027-02-11.
- Lena: open infra change for memcache hardening, schedule maintenance, and add test to staging hardening checklist. Due 2027-02-15.
- Samir: create allowlist rules for secret scanner false positives; file follow-up in RED-5770. Due 2027-02-14.
- Eve: draft secrets rotation enforcement change with comms template. Due 2027-02-18.
- Maya + Lena: threat model diagram + HSM attestation requirements doc. Due 2027-02-23.
- Jo Ramos (SRE): prototype rotation-events aggregator for observability. Proposal due 2027-02-17.
- Maya: loop in Legal (Priya) for privacy language review of KMS onboarding API. Ping by 2027-02-10.

8) Misc notes / questions to surface in wider forum
- Should we require mandatory 2FA for all infra console logins that access wrapped keys, even for internal engineers? (consensus: yes for high-sensitivity roles; define role list)
- Evaluate short-lived developer credentials for common workflows — will break some scripts; we need a migration plan.
- Consider running a red-team micro-exercise focused on Private deployment onboarding (simulate malicious customer key provisioning).

9) Next meeting prep
- Bring updated PR status for RED-5412 and CHANGE-1182
- Have Eve present a short primer on the new rotation policy (2–3 slides)
- Bring a draft of the threat model diagram (Maya + Lena)

Raw notes / one-liners captured during sync:
- "scanner caught gist at 03:12 UTC, blocked before wide exposure"
- "can we make wrap-only keys mandatory for private images?"
- "memcache default creds story is worse in staging parity than we thought"

---
Informal closing: this doc is intentionally rough; I will convert to a cleaned action tracker and push to Confluence if reviewers want a formal record. Otherwise we keep as a living working note in Drive.

File history: draft capture by Maya Chen during sync; minor edits 2027-02-10 to add owners and dates.
